correctness.rationale: The source proof is reconstructible: product algebra C=k⊕V⊕W⊕V⊗W has radical M, M²=V⊗W and M³=0. Since (v+w)²=2v⊗w and char(k) !=2, the intrinsic square-zero locus in M/M² is V union W. For m≠n every augmented algebra automorphism fixes both pieces; its restriction to M² is S⊗T, and intertwining the two oriented operators forces id⊗R=Q⊗id and thus Q=R=cI with c(c+lambda)=0. For m=n, tensor-operator ranks force rank Q=rank R; the relation Q(Q+lambda I)=0 means equal-rank operators are similar, via square-zero Jordan blocks at lambda=0 and 0/-lambda eigenspace decompositions otherwise. The induced factor isomorphisms construct reverse-order isomorphisms. The smallest strictly intermediate balanced example m=2,n=4,ranks1,2 has total dimension15 and rank7 on either order. The finite checker verified tensor rank formulas on four independently constructed examples, but the universal statement rests on the algebraic proof.

value.rationale: Classifying all reversal isomorphisms, rather than the ordinary flip alone, isolates an intrinsic multiplication obstruction invisible to linear-operator rank and resolves the mathematically motivated fixed-intermediate-ratio braiding question for full monoidal subcategories. The 15-dimensional positive-rank boundary is a sharp natural witness.

final_claim: For char(k) != 2, square-zero augmentations of dimensions m,n >=1, Q(Q+lambda I)=R(R+lambda I)=0: opposite oriented tensor products are isomorphic exactly when m=n and rank Q=rank R, or when m!=n and Q,R are both zero or both -lambda times the identity. A 15-dimensional weight-zero pair has equal tensor-operator ranks seven and is linearly similar yet not isomorphic as augmented Rota–Baxter algebras; all intermediate rational rank ratios give similar obstacles to full-subcategory braiding.
